note: Shabbat Companion data, written for Aleph. It adds nothing to the liturgy: every Hebrew line is read from data/corpus/registry.json by id, and the service order itself is data/service/orders.json (friday-night, shabbat-morning). No prayerbook text, layout, page numbers or arrangement wording is used (for example Mishkan T'filah). The order, the choice of congregational responses and the home-ritual steps are NOT reviewed by a rabbi, cantor or Hebrew educator.

review.label: Order not yet reviewed by a rabbi

drills.title: Barchu: The Response
drills.how: The leader calls the congregation to bless. Everyone answers with the second line.

drills.title: The Sh'ma
drills.how: In many congregations the leader begins and everyone joins in. Hear the first word, then come in with the whole line.

drills.title: After the Sh'ma: The Quiet Line
drills.how: After the Sh'ma line, the next line is usually said quietly.

drills.title: Mi Chamocha
drills.how: Mi Chamocha is usually sung together. Hear the first word, then come in with the whole line.

drills.title: Kaddish: The Big Response
drills.how: The Kaddish line ends with an invitation to say Amen. Answer Amen, then the response line.

drills.title: Kaddish: Amen
drills.how: Several Kaddish lines end with an invitation to say Amen. Answer when the line ends.

drills.title: Gadlu: The Answer
drills.how: When the ark is open, the leader says Gadlu and the congregation answers with Lecha (the service guide names the leader's line and the congregation's line).

drills.title: Kedushah: The Three Verses
drills.how: During the leader's repetition of the Amidah the congregation joins the Kedushah responses (the service guide). Aleph does not hold the leader's lines between the verses yet, so hear the first word, then come in with the three verses.

home.title: Kiddush over Wine or Grape Juice
